chunks: Al-Hasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The one who makes a bequest has the right to go back on it and make changes in his bequest as long as he is alive.

key_terms.أَنْ يَرْجِعَ فِيهَا: To revoke or go back on the bequest.
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: A bequest or will made concerning one's property or instructions after death.
key_terms.لِصَاحِبِ الْوَصِيَّةِ: The person who made the will and retains authority over it during life.
key_terms.مَا دَامَ حَيًّا: As long as he is alive.
key_terms.وَيُحْدِثَ فِي وَصِيَّتِهِ: To introduce changes or amendments into the will.

ai.seo_question: Can a person revoke or change his will while still alive in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding a bequest: the person who made the will retains authority over it during his lifetime. He may revoke it or amend it so long as he remains alive, showing that the bequest does not become irrevocably fixed before death.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5457 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faḍḍal narrated from Ali ibn Uqbah from Burayd Al-ʿIjli from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:
"The one who makes a will has the right to revoke it or make changes to it as long as he is alive."
